        ### Question
        An investigator studying fungal growth isolates organisms from an infant with diaper rash. The isolate is cultured and exposed to increasing concentrations of nystatin. Selected colonies continue to grow and replicate even at high concentrations of the drug. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this finding?

        ### Options
        opa. Reduced ergosterol content in cell membrane
opb. Inactivation of cytosine permease
opc. Mutation of the β-glucan gene
opd. Altered binding site of squalene epoxidase
ope. Expression of dysfunctional cytochrome P-450 enzymes

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Reduced ergosterol content in cell membrane -> Decreased susceptibility to nystatin -> Fungal growth continues even at high drug concentrations -> 80%
CHAIN: Inactivation of cytosine permease -> Decreased drug uptake by the fungal cells -> Reduced effectiveness of nystatin -> Continued growth at high drug concentrations -> 75%
CHAIN: Mutation of the β-glucan gene -> Altered cell wall composition -> Decreased nystatin binding affinity -> Continued growth despite high drug concentrations -> 70%
CHAIN: Altered binding site of squalene epoxidase -> Impaired ergosterol synthesis pathway -> Reduced dependency on ergosterol for membrane integrity -> Continued growth in the presence of nystatin -> 65%
CHAIN: Expression of dysfunctional cytochrome P-450 enzymes -> Impaired drug metabolism -> Reduced intracellular drug concentration -> Continued fungal growth at high nystatin levels -> 60%
